findings.issue: D-3 says the advice block keeps engine hand state out of the advice code bots can reach. ADVICE_BOUNDARY_PATTERNS only checks specifiers that contain 'engine/'. Any advice file can still import project modules that hold or build hand state: src/table/session.ts (TableState.hand: HandState, botTurn() returns {hand}, dealHand, applyBotDecision), src/table/hint.ts (functions that take HandState), src/playtest/runner.ts and style-check.ts (createHand/applyAction), and src/storage/hand-store.ts (sharedHandStore(), whose stored records carry replayCode). That is exactly the drift D-3 is meant to stop, one hop further away.
findings.evidence: Future or faulty advice code (the path D-3 guards) -> src/advice/x.ts `import { dealHand, botTurn, type TableState } from '../table/session'` -> session.ts imports createHand/applyAction/HandState/shuffledDeck -> bot imports ../advice/x and gets hand-state helpers and types. Checked in-process with the repo config: `import { dealHand, type TableState } from '../table/session'` and `import { botTurn } from '../table/session'` linted as src/advice/q*.ts give zero errors.
findings.fix: Turn the advice block into an allow-list. Today advice imports only './…' siblings and the five engine modules (grep of src/advice), so add a pattern such as { regex: '^\.\./(?!engine/)', message: ADVICE_BOUNDARY_MESSAGE }, or an explicit ban on '(^|/)(table|playtest|storage|stats|bots|ui)(/|$)'. Add a failing sandbox probe, e.g. src/advice/probe-table.ts importing '../table/session'.

findings.issue: BOT_BOUNDARY_PATTERNS only restricts 'engine/*' (plus advice/golden and packages). Bots can import src/table, src/playtest and src/storage directly, and those modules expose hand state. src/bots/lineup.ts already imports from ../table/session. This brings back the AC#1 gap through another module: `import('../table/session').TableState` (or `import type { TableState }`) gives a bot HandState through TableState['hand'] and BotTurn.hand. At runtime, `sharedHandStore()` from ../storage/hand-store gives a bot the IndexedDB records of past hands, including replay codes (opponents' mucked cards, which REQ-029.3 also forbids). It also gets round the headless no-restricted-globals ban on indexedDB. This was already missing before this change (TASK-6.21), but it is the direct path the caller asked about, and this change does not close it.
findings.evidence: Bot code -> `import { sharedHandStore } from '../storage/hand-store'` / `import type { TableState } from '../table/session'` / `export type H = import('../table/session').TableState` / `import { hintArrived } from '../table/hint'` / `import { runHands } from '../playtest/runner'`. Each, linted in-process as src/bots/p*.ts with the repo config, gives zero errors. tsc (bundler resolution) resolves them and accepts TableState['hand'].
findings.fix: Make the bot boundary an allow-list of project modules: './…' (bots), '../advice/<not golden>', '../engine/player-view' (types), '../engine/hand' (Action/SeatNumber/Street). Allow '../table/session' only as a type import with allowImportNames ['LineUpName','SessionConfig','SessionSeat'] (what lineup.ts uses), and ban other table/playtest/storage/stats imports. Give TSImportType the same allow-list (for example a selector on TSImportType[source.value=/^\.\.\/(?!engine\/|advice\/)/]). If this is judged out of scope for TASK-6.27, record it as a follow-up task rather than dropping it.

findings.issue: The bot ban on advice/golden is anchored at '(^|/)advice/golden$'. With moduleResolution 'bundler', '../advice/golden.js' resolves to golden.ts and typechecks, but does not match the pattern. Type-position `import('../advice/golden').X` is also not checked, because BOT_TYPE_IMPORT_SYNTAX covers only engine paths. golden.ts holds no live-hand state (it builds fixed test hands), so a bot gets createHand-based helpers but no hidden cards. Defence in depth only.
findings.evidence: src/bots/p4.ts `import { parseGoldenSpots } from '../advice/golden.js'` -> zero lint errors (in-process), and tsc resolves it. `export type G = import('../advice/golden').GoldenSpot` -> zero errors.
findings.fix: Use regex '(^|/)advice/golden(\.[cm]?[jt]s)?$' and add a matching TSImportType selector. Optionally reject '.js'/'.ts' extensions on project specifiers in bots and advice altogether.

findings.issue: golden.ts is outside the advice boundary, but nothing stops a bot-reachable advice file from importing or re-exporting './golden'. That gives bots a transitive path to the module the bot-side ban is meant to keep away from them. golden holds no live-hand state, so this is drift protection only.
findings.evidence: src/advice/q2.ts `import { parseGoldenSpots } from './golden'; export { parseGoldenSpots };` -> zero lint errors; a bot importing ../advice/q2 then reaches golden (createHand/applyAction/playerView).
findings.fix: Add { regex: '(^|/)golden(\.[cm]?[jt]s)?$', message: ADVICE_BOUNDARY_MESSAGE } to ADVICE_BOUNDARY_PATTERNS. golden.ts is ignored by the block, and tests/golden sit outside src/advice, so nothing legitimate breaks.

findings.issue: Advice files can still write `import('../engine/hand').HandState` in type position (the spec deliberately leaves this out). Types cannot carry runtime data, and a bot has no HandState value to pass, so there is no leak. But an advice helper with a HandState-typed signature is the first step of the drift D-3 describes.
findings.evidence: src/advice/q5.ts `export type H = import('../engine/hand').HandState;` -> zero lint errors.
findings.fix: Optional: add 'no-restricted-syntax' to adviceHiddenStateConfig, with TSImportType selectors like BOT_TYPE_IMPORT_SYNTAX (allowing the advice engine allow-list). It must also repeat BOT_DETERMINISM_RESTRICTED_SYNTAX, because the block would replace that rule's options for src/advice/**.

summary: The AC#1 TSImportType selectors work as specified: engine/hand non-allow-listed qualifiers, typeof import, other engine modules, .ts/.js extensions and non-normalized paths all fail. The advice engine-import rules also work, including export *, namespace imports, export-from and .ts extensions. The main gap is that both boundaries only look at 'engine/*' specifiers. Advice code (MAJOR) and bot code (MAJOR, already missing before this change) can import src/table/session, src/table/hint, src/playtest/runner and src/storage/hand-store, which hold or build HandState, TableState.hand and stored replay codes. So D-3's 'hand state stays out of bot-reachable advice' holds only one import hop deep. No live leak exists today, because bots get only a PlayerView at runtime and no TableState value. One exception: storage/hand-store's sharedHandStore() is a runtime path to past hands' records. Minor: the golden ban can be bypassed with a '.js' extension, a type-position import or an advice re-export. No new dependencies, secrets or randomness.
